summary: WSL-to-Windows persistence dropper hidden in calendar utility package
details: nolby advertises itself as a calendar-day/streak math library but ships a 256KB Windows PE executable disguised as cache.dat and, at module top-level in index.mjs, runs a hidden async _sync() routine on every import. When executed on Linux with /mnt/c present (a WSL environment), _sync() enumerates Windows user profiles under /mnt/c/Users, locates the Windows Startup folder (AppData/Roaming/Microsoft/Windows/Start Menu/Programs/Startup), and writes cache.dat to that folder as vite-native-helper.exe. On the next Windows login the planted PE runs automatically, giving the package author code execution on the Windows host that owns the WSL instance. The filename impersonates a Vite build helper, the executable is undocumented in README, and the drop fires as a side effect of import with no user interaction.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
